p8_b0.ocr: Table 1 presents data on various biochemical markers in two groups: Air and Wood smoke. The Reduced GSH (μM/mg protein) is 25.9 (19.3 - 29.3) for Air and 22.8 (20.2 - 27.5) for Wood smoke. The percentage of GSSG is 7.4 (4.5-9.9) in Air compared to 9.0 (6.6-15.8) in Wood smoke. Ascorbate levels (μM/mg protein) are 8.07 (6.35 - 10.1) for Air and 8.02 (6.67 - 10.2) for Wood smoke. The percentage of DHA is 23.1 (17.5-32.9) in Air and 23.0 (15.4-33.0) in Wood smoke.

p8_b1.ocr: Urate levels (μM/mg protein) are 1.59 (1.09 - 2.24) in Air versus 1.80 (0.11 - 2.85) in Wood smoke. HO-1 (ng/mg protein) measures 7.32 (4.48 - 9.95) in Air and 7.52 (5.34 - 9.89) in Wood smoke. Total Protein (mg/ml) is 0.12 (0.09 - 0.16) for both groups, and Glutathione S-transferase (U/mg protein) is 0.55 (0.39 - 0.82) for Air and 0.59 (0.37 - 0.84) for Wood smoke. Table 2 details demographic and clinical characteristics across five groups: Controls, Inactive UC, Active UC, Inactive CD, and Active CD. The sample sizes are 10, 5, 6, 5, and 2 respectively.
